newsitem.title: USA: U.S. PLAINS FED CATTLE BIDS $64, PASSED - FEEDLOTS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. PLAINS FED CATTLE BIDS $64, PASSED - FEEDLOTS.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle bids early Wednesday were at $64.00 per cwt, unchanged from light activity on Tuesday, and they were being passed by owners pricing cattle at $65.00 to mostly $66.00, feedlot sources said.
"A bid at $65.00 will buy a lot of cattle," a Texas Panhandle feedlot operator said.
Cattle owners were optimistic that active beef movement Tuesday, albeit at lower prices, would spur increased packer demand and result in the firm fed cattle prices, several cattle feeders said.

Beef prices on Tuesday were quoted down $0.12 to $0.34 per cwt, with 259 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA reported. Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $102.84, down $0.34 compared with Monday, the statistics showed.
Attempts at getting higher fed cattle prices were stymied by packers' continued reliance on contract and formula contract supplies, said Dale Benson, livestock analyst with Dean-Witter Reynolds.
Benson said the reliance on contract cattle was strong last week, which resulted in many showlists not selling out.
